Four panes, one source. Every pane compiles it; none rejects the resources
declared inside the constant buffers.

What to compare is the "Buffer Definitions" comment block that FXC and the two
DXC panes print, and specifically the Offset column of the scalar field that
follows each buffer member, plus the Size reported for each constant buffer.

FXC (ps_5_0) places that scalar field at offset 0 in all four constant buffers
and reports each of them as 4 bytes.

Both DXC panes place it at offset 12 in the second constant buffer and at offset
64 in the third, and report those two buffers as 16 and 68 bytes: a
StructuredBuffer member consumes the size of its element type in the constant
buffer. The fourth buffer, whose member is a typed Buffer rather than a
StructuredBuffer, is laid out the way FXC lays it out.

So the same source produces two different host-side constant-buffer layouts, and
neither compiler says anything about it.

The clang-dxc pane runs the front end only. Its diagnostics are all about the
implicit uint-to-float4 conversions in the return statement, which is what shows
that Sema did resolve the members of all four buffers; it says nothing about the
resources inside them.

Note the Resource Bindings table: the buffers are never read in this shader, so
neither compiler emits a t# binding for them. The 1.6 pane's remark about a
missing DXIL.dll is Compiler Explorer's environment, not this shader.

Local evidence -- 20 stable DXC releases, the DXIL validator's verdict on the
container, and the reflection the runtime would see -- is in the issue's triage
directory.
